summary: Flathead National Forest steel tower with a tent cabin, built in 1934 and later abandoned; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Abandoned and listed as gone. No source we read describes the site today.

events.note: Steel tower with tent cabin, per firelookout.com
Abandoned; the site page gives no year

evidence.supports: built 1934; steel tower with tent cabin
fire-detection points on high peaks after the 1910 fire season
evidence.quote: After the 1910 fire season, the Forest Service went on the offensive, setting up fire detection points on high peaks

evidence.supports: lookouts added especially in the 1930s; 147 lookouts and towers by 1939
evidence.quote: The Forest built more and more lookouts, especially during the 1930s, until in 1939 there were 147 lookouts and towers on the Flathead National Forest

evidence.supports: list places the site in Flathead County and marks it as a gone tower

sources.title: Trails of the Past: Historical Overview of the Flathead National Forest, Montana, 1800-1960, Chapter 9

notes_for_editor: Almost every fact rests on one line of the firelookout.com page (1934, steel tower with tent cabin, abandoned, gone); the Forest Association list row confirms only the Flathead County location, the tower type and gone status. The page gives no abandonment year, so the abandonment event has no year. Two web searches and the Flathead history chapter found no staffing, fire or present-day site records. The record coordinates match the list row.
